title: Merge Two Search Trees Into One Sorted List

concept.title: Two sorted lists from two in-order walks, then the merge step
body: The in-order walk of a binary search tree is a **sorted list**. So the sorted list of all values of two search trees is the merge of two sorted lists, the same "merge" step as in merge sort: keep an index in each list, and always take the smaller of the two current values.

body.code:
x, y = in_order(a), in_order(b)
result = []
i = j = 0
while i < len(x) and j < len(y):
    if x[i] <= y[j]:
        result.append(x[i])
        i += 1
    else:
        result.append(y[j])
        j += 1
result += x[i:] + y[j:]            # one of the two is empty; the other one still has its tail

body: The walks are O(n + m) and the merge is O(n + m), so the whole is linear: much better than putting everything in one list and sorting it (O((n + m) log (n + m))). The same idea is in "merge two sorted lists" and in the merge step of merge sort: whenever the inputs are already sorted, use their order.

statement: Two binary search trees are given. Print all their values in increasing order on one line (a value that is in both trees is printed twice).
inputFormat: The first two lines describe the first tree and the next two lines describe the second tree. A tree is described by a line with the number of words `t`, and a line with the tree in level order (the root first, then the children row by row from left to right, `N` for a missing child, no `N` at the end).
outputFormat: All the values in increasing order on one line.
constraints: 1 <= number of nodes of each tree <= 20000
The height of each tree is at most 800.
Both trees are binary search trees; inside one tree all values are different, but the same value may be in both trees.

examples.note: The trees have the values 1 2 4 and 0 1 3: 0 1 1 2 3 4.

hints: An in-order walk of a search tree gives its values in increasing order.
Write both lists, then merge them with one index in each list.
Take the smaller current value each time; when one list ends, copy the rest of the other.

solution.complexity: Time O(n + m), space O(n + m).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def inorder_values(root):
    values = []
    stack = []
    node = root
    while stack or node is not None:
        while node is not None:
            stack.append(node)
            node = node.left
        node = stack.pop()
        values.append(node.val)
        node = node.right
    return values

def merge_trees(first, second):
    x, y = inorder_values(first), inorder_values(second)
    result = []
    i = j = 0
    while i < len(x) and j < len(y):
        if x[i] <= y[j]:
            result.append(x[i])
            i += 1
        else:
            result.append(y[j])
            j += 1
    return result + x[i:] + y[j:]

t = int(input())
a = input().split()
u = int(input())
b = input().split()

print(*merge_trees(build_tree(a), build_tree(b)))
